sources_considered.why: Independent contemporary evaluation, but without the training-input comparison needed to settle diminishing returns.
Retrospective analysis specifically examines early-2025 models and expected scaling.
Confirms the report's September 16, 2025 publication date and Google DeepMind commission.
Launch claims and descriptions of changed training methods do not supply a controlled cross-generation return curve.

evidence_items.explanation: METR found limited relative performance on its autonomy and research-engineering evaluations. This does not measure gains per unit of training input.

The footnote compares GPT-4.5 benchmark improvements with historical gains per order of magnitude of compute. This challenges a new breakdown in scaling, but expected scaling can itself have diminishing marginal returns.

unresolved_gaps: No matched series establishes a broad decline in gains per added training input during the target period.
The claim does not distinguish ordinary diminishing marginal returns from a newly emerging slowdown.
The retrieved evidence does not cover deep learning beyond frontier language models.
